    protected static ExpressionParsingState composeBinaryOperationExpression(
            final ExpressionParsingState state, final int nodeIndex, final String[] operators,
            final boolean[] leniencies, final Class<? extends BinaryOperationExpression>[] operationClasses,
            final Method leftAllowedMethod, final Method rightAllowedMethod) {

        // Returning "state" means "try next in chain" or "success"
        // Returning "null" means parsing error
        //
        // "Lenient" means that if the last operator occurrence found does not result
        // in a valid parse result, the previous-to-last (and all previous to that)
        // should also be tried in sequence (this is mainly to avoid "-" symbols from
        // minus operators getting in the way of subtraction operations).

        final String input = state.get(nodeIndex).getInput();

        if (StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(input)) {
            return null;
        }

        String scannedInput = input.toLowerCase(); 

        do {
            
            int operatorIndex = -1;
            int operatorPosFrom = -1;
            int operatorPosTo = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
            int operatorLen = 0;
            
            for (int i = 0; i < operators.length; i++) {
                // Trying to fail quickly...
                final int currentOperatorPosFrom = scannedInput.lastIndexOf(operators[i]);
                if (currentOperatorPosFrom != -1) {
                    final int currentOperatorLen = operators[i].length();
                    final int currentOperatorPosTo = currentOperatorPosFrom + currentOperatorLen;
                    if (operatorPosFrom == -1 || operatorPosTo < currentOperatorPosFrom || 
                            (currentOperatorLen > operatorLen && currentOperatorPosTo >= operatorPosTo)) {
                        // the last condition is for allowing "<=" not to be confused with "<" or "neq" with "eq"
                        operatorPosFrom = currentOperatorPosFrom;
                        operatorLen = operators[i].length();
                        operatorPosTo = currentOperatorPosFrom + operatorLen;
                        operatorIndex = i;
                    }
                }

            if (operatorPosFrom == -1) {
                return state;

                        state, nodeIndex, operators[operatorIndex], operationClasses[operatorIndex],
                        leftAllowedMethod, rightAllowedMethod, input, operatorPosFrom) == null) {

                if (leniencies[operatorIndex]) {
                    scannedInput = scannedInput.substring(0, operatorPosFrom);
                } else {
                    return null;
                }

            } else {
                return state;
            }

    static Expression parse(final String input) {

        Validate.notNull(input, "Input cannot be null");

        /*
         * PHASE 01: Decomposition (including unnesting parenthesis)
         */
        final ExpressionParsingState decomposition = ExpressionParsingUtil.decompose(input);
        if (decomposition == null) {
            return null;
        }

        /*
         * PHASE 02: Composition
         */
        final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(decomposition);
        if (result == null || !result.hasExpressionAt(0)) {
            return null;
        }

        return result.get(0).getExpression();

    }
    

    
    

    
    
    
    
    static Object execute(
            final IExpressionContext context,
            final Expression expression, final IStandardVariableExpressionEvaluator expressionEvaluator,
            final StandardExpressionExecutionContext expContext) {

            return SimpleExpression.executeSimple(context, (SimpleExpression)expression, expressionEvaluator, expContext);

        if (expression instanceof ComplexExpression) {
            return ComplexExpression.executeComplex(context, (ComplexExpression)expression, expContext);
        }

        throw new TemplateProcessingException("Unrecognized expression: " + expression.getClass().getName());
        
    }

package org.thymeleaf.standard.expression;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertInstanceOf;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertSame;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;


/**
 * Unit tests for {@code ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(ExpressionParsingState, int)}.
 *
 * The behaviour of the method is observed through the state it returns (or the {@code null} it
 * returns on error), the expression placed at the composed node, and the expressions that are
 * produced for each of the supported expression kinds.
 */
public class ExpressionParsingUtilComposeTests {


    private static String placeholder(final int index) {
        return String.valueOf(Expression.PARSING_PLACEHOLDER_CHAR) + index + String.valueOf(Expression.PARSING_PLACEHOLDER_CHAR);
    }


    private static ExpressionParsingState stateOf(final String... nodeInputs) {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = new ExpressionParsingState();
        for (final String nodeInput : nodeInputs) {
            state.addNode(nodeInput);
        }
        return state;
    }


    private static ExpressionParsingState decomposeState(final String input) {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = ExpressionParsingUtil.decompose(input);
        assertNotNull(state, "Decomposition should succeed for input: " + input);
        return state;
    }


    private static Expression composeInput(final String input) {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = decomposeState(input);
        final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(state, 0);
        assertNotNull(result, "Composition should succeed for input: " + input);
        assertTrue(result.hasExpressionAt(0), "Node 0 should hold an expression for input: " + input);
        return result.get(0).getExpression();
    }


    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Invalid state / node index handling
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @Test
    @DisplayName("compose() returns null for a null state")
    public void composeReturnsNullForNullState() {
...
    public void composeReturnsNullWhenNoExpressionTypeMatches() {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = decomposeState("abc def");

        assertNull(ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(state, 0));
        assertTrue(state.hasStringAt(0));
        assertFalse(state.hasExpressionAt(0));
    }


    @Test
    @DisplayName("public compose(state) composes the root node")
    public void publicComposeComposesRootNode() {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = decomposeState("1 + 2");

        final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(state);

        assertSame(state, result);
        assertTrue(result.hasExpressionAt(0));
        assertInstanceOf(AdditionExpression.class, result.get(0).getExpression());
        assertEquals("1 + 2", result.get(0).getExpression().getStringRepresentation());
    }


    @Test
    @DisplayName("compose() on the root of a decomposed expression composes all referenced leaf nodes")
    public void composeComposesReferencedLeafNodesAsWell() {
        final ExpressionParsingState state = decomposeState("${a} + ${b}");

        assertTrue(state.size() > 1);
        final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(state, 0);

        assertNotNull(result);
        assertTrue(result.hasExpressionAt(0));
        for (int i = 1; i < result.size(); i++) {
            assertTrue(result.hasExpressionAt(i), "Leaf node " + i + " should have been composed");
        }
    }


}

    private static Expression parseDefaultAsLiteral(final String input) {

        if (StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(input)) {
            return null;
        }

        final Expression expr = Expression.parse(input);
        if (expr == null) {
            return Expression.parse(TextLiteralExpression.wrapStringIntoLiteral(input));
        }
        return expr;

    }





    private static int indexOfLastParenthesesGroup(final String input) {

        final int inputLen = input.length();
        final char finalC = input.charAt(inputLen - 1);
        if (finalC != ')') {
            // If there are parentheses, the last char must be an ending one.
            return -1;
        }
        boolean inLiteral = false;
        int parenLevel = 1;
        for (int i = inputLen - 2; i >= 0; i--) {
            final char c = input.charAt(i);
            if (c == '(' && !inLiteral) {
                parenLevel--;
                if (parenLevel == 0) {
                    // We have closed a parenthesis at level 0, this might be what we were looking for.
                    if (i == (inputLen - 2)) {
                        // These are not real parameters, but "()", which might be a "text()" node selector.
                        return -1;
                    }
                    return i;
                }
            } else if (c == ')' && !inLiteral) {
                parenLevel++;
            } else if (c == '\'' && !TextLiteralExpression.isDelimiterEscaped(input, i)) {
                inLiteral = !inLiteral;
            }
        }
        // Cannot parse: will never be able to determine whether there are parameters or not, because they aren't
        // correctly closed. Just return -1 as if we didn't find parentheses at all.
        return -1;

    }


    private static AssignationSequence createSyntheticallyNamedParameterSequence(final ExpressionSequence expSeq) {

        final List<Assignation> assignations = new ArrayList<Assignation>(expSeq.size() + 2);

        int argIndex = 0;
        for (final IStandardExpression expression : expSeq.getExpressions()) {
            final IStandardExpression parameterName =
                    Expression.parse(TextLiteralExpression.wrapStringIntoLiteral(UNNAMED_PARAMETERS_PREFIX + argIndex++));
            assignations.add(new Assignation(parameterName, expression));
        }

        return new AssignationSequence(assignations);

    }

        if (!(context instanceof ITemplateContext)) {

                    "Cannot evaluate expression \"" + expression + "\". Fragment expressions " +
                    "can only be evaluated in a template-processing environment (as a part of an in-template expression) " +
                    "where processing context is an implementation of " + ITemplateContext.class.getClass() + ", which it isn't (" +
                    context.getClass().getName() + ")");
        }

        if (expression == EMPTY_FRAGMENT_EXPRESSION) {
            return Fragment.EMPTY_FRAGMENT;

                false);

* * @author Daniel Fernández * * @since 3.0.0 * */ public abstract class Expression implements IStandardExpression, Serializable { private static final long serialVersionUID = 1608378943284014151L; public static final char PARSING_PLACEHOLDER_CHAR = '\u00A7'; public static final char NESTING_START_CHAR = '('; public static final char NESTING_END_CHAR = ')'; protected Expression() { super(); } public abstract String getStringRepresentation(); @Override public String toString() { return getStringRepresentation(); } static Expression parse(final String input) { Validate.notNull(input, "Input cannot be null"); /* * PHASE 01: Decomposition (including unnesting parenthesis) */ final ExpressionParsingState decomposition = ExpressionParsingUtil.decompose(input); if (decomposition == null) { return null; } /* * PHASE 02: Composition */ final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(decomposition); if (result == null || !result.hasExpressionAt(0)) { return null; } return result.get(0).getExpression(); } static Object execute( final IExpressionContext context, final Expression expression, final IStandardVariableExpressionEvaluator expressionEvaluator, final StandardExpressionExecutionContext expContext) { if (expression instanceof SimpleExpression) { return SimpleExpression.executeSimple(context, (SimpleExpression)expression, expressionEvaluator, expContext); } if (expression instanceof ComplexExpression) { return ComplexExpression.executeComplex(context, (ComplexExpression)expression, expContext); } throw new TemplateProcessingException("Unrecognized expression: " + expression.getClass().getName()); }

        @Test
        public void fragmentSpecificationContainingUnparsableTextBecomesATextLiteral() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("t :: f (a=1) extra");

            assertEquals("t", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getFragmentSelector());
            assertEquals("'f (a=1) extra'", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertEquals("~{t :: 'f (a=1) extra'}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
            assertNull(expression.getParameters());
        }


        @Test
        public void onlyTheLastParenthesesGroupIsConsideredAsTheParametersGroup() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("tmpl :: frag (a=1) :: other");

            assertEquals("tmpl", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getFragmentSelector());
            assertEquals("'frag (a=1) :: other'", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertNull(expression.getParameters());
            assertFalse(expression.hasParameters());
        }


        @Test
        public void multipleParenthesesGroupsOnlyUseTheLastOneAsParameters() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("t :: f (a=1,b=2) (c=3)");

            assertEquals("t", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertEquals("'f (a=1,b=2)'", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertEquals(Arrays.asList("c=3"), assignationsOf(expression));
            assertFalse(expression.hasSyntheticParameters());
            assertEquals("~{t :: 'f (a=1,b=2)' (c=3)}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        }


        @Test
        public void unterminatedParenthesisIsKeptAsPartOfTheFragmentSpecification() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("template :: frag (");

            assertEquals("template", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertEquals("'frag ('", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertNull(expression.getParameters());
            assertEquals("~{template :: 'frag ('}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        }


        @Test
        public void tildeWrapperIsNotRemovedByTheContentParser() {
            // Removing the ~{...} wrapper is the responsibility of parseFragmentExpression(), not of this method
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("~{template :: frag}");

            assertEquals("'~{template'", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertEquals("'frag}'", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertEquals("~{'~{template' :: 'frag}'}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        }


    }

        @ParameterizedTest(name = "input [{0}]")
        @ValueSource(strings = {"template :: frag ()", "t :: f ()"})
        public void emptyParenthesesAreNotConsideredParameters(final String input) {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse(input);

            final String expectedSelector = "'" + input.substring(input.indexOf("::") + 2).trim() + "'";
            assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getFragmentSelector());
            assertEquals(expectedSelector, representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertNull(expression.getParameters());
            assertFalse(expression.hasParameters());
            assertEquals("~{" + input.substring(0, input.indexOf("::")).trim() + " :: " + expectedSelector + "}",
                    expression.getStringRepresentation());
        }


        @ParameterizedTest(name = "input [{0}]")
        @ValueSource(strings = {"(1,2)", "(a=1)"})
        public void parenthesesGroupAloneIsTreatedAsTheTemplateName(final String input) {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse(input);

            assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getTemplateName());
            assertEquals(input, representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertEquals("~{'" + input + "'}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
            assertNull(expression.getFragmentSelector());
            assertEquals("'" + input + "'", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
        }


        @Test
        public void parenthesesGroupAfterTemplateNameWithoutSeparatorAreParameters() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("template (a=1)");

            assertEquals("~{template (a=1)}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
            assertEquals("template", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertNull(expression.getFragmentSelector());
            assertFalse(expression.hasFragmentSelector());
            assertEquals(Arrays.asList("a=1"), assignationsOf(expression));
            assertFalse(expression.hasSyntheticParameters());
        }


        @Test
        public void parenthesesGroupContainingParenthesesAndSeparatorIsALiteralTemplateName() {
            final FragmentExpression expression = parse("(a=1) :: f");

            assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getTemplateName());
            assertEquals("'(a=1)'", representationOf(expression.getTemplateName()));
            assertEquals("f", representationOf(expression.getFragmentSelector()));
            assertNull(expression.getParameters());

import java.util.List;

import org.thymeleaf.util.Validate;



/**

 * 
 * @since 1.1
 *
 */
public final class AssignationSequence implements Iterable<Assignation>, Serializable {

    
    private static final long serialVersionUID = -4915282307441011014L;


    private final List<Assignation> assignations;
    
    
    
    AssignationSequence(final List<Assignation> assignations) {
        super();
        Validate.notNull(assignations, "Assignation list cannot be null");
        Validate.containsNoNulls(assignations, "Assignation list cannot contain any nulls");
        this.assignations = Collections.unmodifiableList(assignations);
    }

    
    public List<Assignation> getAssignations() {
        return this.assignations;
    }
  
    public int size() {
        return this.assignations.size();
    }
    
    public Iterator<Assignation> iterator() {
        return this.assignations.iterator();
    }

    
    public String getStringRepresentation() {
        final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        if (this.assignations.size() > 0) {
            sb.append(this.assignations.get(0));
            for (int i = 1; i < this.assignations.size(); i++) {
                sb.append(',');
                sb.append(this.assignations.get(i));
            }
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return getStringRepresentation();
    }

    
    

}

package org.thymeleaf.standard.expression;

import java.io.Serializable;

import org.thymeleaf.util.Validate;



/**
 * 
 * @author Daniel Fernández
 * 
 * @since 1.1
 *
 */
public final class Assignation implements Serializable {

    private static final long serialVersionUID = -20278893925937213L;
    

    private final IStandardExpression left;
    private final IStandardExpression right;
         
    
    Assignation(final IStandardExpression left, final IStandardExpression right) {
        super();
        Validate.notNull(left, "Assignation left side cannot be null");
        this.left = left;
        this.right = right;
    }



    public IStandardExpression getLeft() {
        return this.left;
    }

    public IStandardExpression getRight() {
        return this.right;
    }
    
    public String getStringRepresentation() {
        final StringBuilder strBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        strBuilder.append(this.left.getStringRepresentation());
        if (this.right != null) {
            strBuilder.append('=');
            if (this.right instanceof ComplexExpression) {
                strBuilder.append('(');
                strBuilder.append(this.right.getStringRepresentation());
                strBuilder.append(')');
            } else {
                strBuilder.append(this.right.getStringRepresentation());
            }
        }
        return strBuilder.toString();
    }


    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return getStringRepresentation();
    }
  
    

    
}

    private static AssignationSequence composeSequence(
            final ExpressionParsingState state, final int nodeIndex, final boolean allowParametersWithoutValue) {

        if (state == null || nodeIndex >= state.size()) {
            return null;
        }

        if (state.hasExpressionAt(nodeIndex)) {
            if (!allowParametersWithoutValue) {
                return null;
            }
            // could happen if we are traversing pointers recursively, so we will consider it a sequence containing
            // only one, no-value assignation (though we will let the Assignation.compose(...) method do the job.
            final Assignation assignation = composeAssignation(state, nodeIndex, allowParametersWithoutValue);
            if (assignation == null) {
                return null;
            }
            final List<Assignation> assignations = new ArrayList<Assignation>(2);
            assignations.add(assignation);
            return new AssignationSequence(assignations);
        }

        final String input = state.get(nodeIndex).getInput();

        if (StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(input)) {
            return null;
        }

        // First, check whether we are just dealing with a pointer input
        final int pointer = ExpressionParsingUtil.parseAsSimpleIndexPlaceholder(input);
        if (pointer != -1) {
            return composeSequence(state, pointer, allowParametersWithoutValue);
        }

        final String[] inputParts = StringUtils.split(input, ",");

        for (final String inputPart : inputParts) {
            // We create new String parsing nodes for all of the elements
            // We add all nodes first so that we know the exact indexes in which they are
            // (composing assignations here can modify the size of the state object without we noticing)
            state.addNode(inputPart.trim());
        }

        final List<Assignation> assignations = new ArrayList<Assignation>(4);
        final int startIndex = state.size() - inputParts.length;
        final int endIndex = state.size();
        for (int i = startIndex; i < endIndex; i++) {
            final Assignation assignation =
                    composeAssignation(state, i, allowParametersWithoutValue);
            if (assignation == null) {
                return null;
            }
            assignations.add(assignation);
        }

        return new AssignationSequence(assignations);

    }




    static Assignation composeAssignation(
            final ExpressionParsingState state, final int nodeIndex, final boolean allowParametersWithoutValue) {

        if (state == null || nodeIndex >= state.size()) {
            return null;
        }

        if (state.hasExpressionAt(nodeIndex)) {
            if (!allowParametersWithoutValue) {
                return null;
            }
            // could happen if we are traversing pointers recursively, so we will consider it a no-value assignation
            return new Assignation(state.get(nodeIndex).getExpression(),null);
        }

        final String input = state.get(nodeIndex).getInput();

        if (StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(input)) {
            return null;
        }

        // First, check whether we are just dealing with a pointer input
        final int pointer = ExpressionParsingUtil.parseAsSimpleIndexPlaceholder(input);
        if (pointer != -1) {
            return composeAssignation(state, pointer, allowParametersWithoutValue);
        }

        final int inputLen = input.length();
        final int operatorPos = input.indexOf('=');

        final String leftInput =
                (operatorPos == -1? input.trim() : input.substring(0,operatorPos).trim());
        final String rightInput =
                (operatorPos == -1 || operatorPos == (inputLen - 1) ? null : input.substring(operatorPos + 1).trim());

        if (StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(leftInput)) {
            return null;
        }

        final Expression leftExpr = ExpressionParsingUtil.parseAndCompose(state, leftInput);
        if (leftExpr == null) {
            return null;
        }

        final Expression rightExpr;
        if (!StringUtils.isEmptyOrWhitespace(rightInput)) {
            rightExpr = ExpressionParsingUtil.parseAndCompose(state, rightInput);
            if (rightExpr == null) {
                return null;
            }
        } else if (!allowParametersWithoutValue) {
            return null;
        } else {
            rightExpr = null;
        }

        return new Assignation(leftExpr, rightExpr);

    }

package org.thymeleaf.standard.expression;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertAll;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertInstanceOf;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNull;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

import java.util.List;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource;


final class LinkExpressionParseLinkExpressionTests {


    @Test
    void returnsNullForNullInput() {
        assertThrows(NullPointerException.class, () -> LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression(null));
    }


    @ParameterizedTest
    @ValueSource(strings = {
            "",
            "plain text",
            "/path",
            "prefix @{/path}",
            "@{/path} suffix",
            "@{unterminated",
            "@{}"
    })
    void returnsNullWhenInputIsNotACompleteLinkExpression(final String input) {
        assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression(input));
    }


    @ParameterizedTest
    @ValueSource(strings = {
            "@{ }",
            "@{\t}",
            "@{\n}",
            "@{ \r\n\t }"
    })
    void returnsNullForWhitespaceOnlyLinkContent(final String input) {
        assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression(input));
    }


    @Test
    void parsesLiteralBaseWithoutParameters() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("  @{ /home/index }  ");

        assertEquals("@{'/home/index'}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'/home/index'", expression.getBase().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getBase());
        assertNull(expression.getParameters());
        assertFalse(expression.hasParameters());
    }


    @Test
    void parsesVariableBaseWithoutParameters() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{${url}}");

        assertEquals("@{${url}}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("${url}", expression.getBase().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(VariableExpression.class, expression.getBase());
        assertNull(expression.getParameters());
        assertFalse(expression.hasParameters());
    }


    @Test
    void parsesParametersIncludingLiteralAndValueLessAssignations() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{/path(foo=${value},bar='literal',flag)}");

        assertEquals("@{'/path'(foo=${value},bar='literal',flag)}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'/path'", expression.getBase().getStringRepresentation());
        assertTrue(expression.hasParameters());

        final AssignationSequence parameters = expression.getParameters();
        assertNotNull(parameters);
        assertEquals(3, parameters.size());

        final List<Assignation> assignations = parameters.getAssignations();

        assertEquals("foo", assignations.get(0).getLeft().getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("${value}", assignations.get(0).getRight().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(VariableExpression.class, assignations.get(0).getRight());

        assertEquals("bar", assignations.get(1).getLeft().getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'literal'", assignations.get(1).getRight().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, assignations.get(1).getRight());

        assertEquals("flag", assignations.get(2).getLeft().getStringRepresentation());
        assertNull(assignations.get(2).getRight());
    }


    @Test
    void trimsWhitespaceAroundBaseAndParameterSpecification() {

        final LinkExpression expression =
                parse("  @{  /path  ( foo = ${value} , bar = 'x' )  }  ");

        assertEquals("@{'/path'(foo=${value},bar='x')}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'/path'", expression.getBase().getStringRepresentation());

        final AssignationSequence parameters = expression.getParameters();
        assertNotNull(parameters);
        assertEquals("foo=${value},bar='x'", parameters.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals(2, parameters.size());
    }


    @Test
    void balancesParenthesesContainedInParameterExpressions() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{/path(foo=${bar},baz=${qux(1)})}");

        assertEquals("@{'/path'(foo=${bar},baz=${qux(1)})}", expression.getStringRepresentation());

        final AssignationSequence parameters = expression.getParameters();
        assertNotNull(parameters);
        assertEquals(2, parameters.size());
        assertEquals("${qux(1)}", parameters.getAssignations().get(1).getRight().getStringRepresentation());
    }


    @Test
    void ignoresParenthesesContainedInTextLiteralParameters() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{/path(param='a)b(c')}");

        assertEquals("@{'/path'(param='a)b(c')}", expression.getStringRepresentation());

        final AssignationSequence parameters = expression.getParameters();
        assertNotNull(parameters);
        assertEquals(1, parameters.size());
        assertEquals("param", parameters.getAssignations().get(0).getLeft().getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'a)b(c'", parameters.getAssignations().get(0).getRight().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, parameters.getAssignations().get(0).getRight());
    }


    @Test
    void doesNotTreatEscapedQuoteAsEndOfTextLiteral() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{/path(param='it\\'s ) ok')}");

        assertEquals("@{'/path'(param='it\\'s ) ok')}", expression.getStringRepresentation());

        final AssignationSequence parameters = expression.getParameters();
        assertNotNull(parameters);
        assertEquals(1, parameters.size());
        assertEquals("param='it\\'s ) ok'", parameters.getStringRepresentation());
    }


    @Test
    void treatsFullyParenthesizedContentAsBaseWhenOpeningParenthesisIsFirst() {

        final LinkExpression expression = parse("@{(http://example.com/path)}");

        assertEquals("@{'(http://example.com/path)'}", expression.getStringRepresentation());
        assertEquals("'(http://example.com/path)'", expression.getBase().getStringRepresentation());
        assertInstanceOf(TextLiteralExpression.class, expression.getBase());
        assertNull(expression.getParameters());
        assertFalse(expression.hasParameters());
    }


    @Test
    void returnsNullForInvalidParameterSpecifications() {
        assertAll(
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path()}")),
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path( )}")),
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path(=bar)}")),
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path(foo=${})}")),
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path(foo='unterminated)}")),
                () -> assertNull(LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression("@{/path(foo))}"))
        );
    }


    private static LinkExpression parse(final String input) {
        final LinkExpression expression = LinkExpression.parseLinkExpression(input);
        assertNotNull(expression, "Expected a link expression to be parsed from: " + input);
        return expression;
    }

}

    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Build file locations       -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <disclaimer-files.basedir>${project.basedir}/../..</disclaimer-files.basedir>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Configure JavaDoc plugin   -->
    <!-- (Avoids JPMS issues.)      -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <maven.javadoc.source>8</maven.javadoc.source>
    <maven.javadoc.release>8</maven.javadoc.release>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- JPMS MODULE management     -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <module.name>TO_BE_SPECIFIED_BY_CHILDREN:module.name</module.name>
  </properties>

  <build>

    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>${disclaimer-files.basedir}</directory>
        <targetPath>META-INF</targetPath>
        <includes>
          <include>LICENSE.txt</include>
          <include>NOTICE.txt</include>
        </includes>
      </resource>
    </resources>

    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
          <configuration>
            <!-- Configuration will be inherited from thymeleaf-parent. At this level we will   -->
            <!-- add some additional properties.                                                -->
            <archive>
              <manifestEntries>
                <!-- Setting this automatic module name will fix the module name used by        -->
                <!-- thymeleaf even if the library is not yet fully modularised.                -->
                <!-- NOTE this will have to be set at each of the modules' pom.xml files.       -->
                <Automatic-Module-Name>${module.name}</Automatic-Module-Name>
              </manifestEntries>
            </archive>
          </configuration>
        </plugin>

          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
          <configuration>
            <show>protected</show>
            <noqualifier>java.lang</noqualifier>
            <source>${maven.javadoc.source}</source>
            <release>${maven.javadoc.release}</release>
            <overview>${basedir}/src/main/javadoc/overview.html</overview>
            <javadocDirectory>${basedir}/src/main/javadoc</javadocDirectory>
            <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}</outputDirectory>
            <doclint>all,-missing</doclint>
          </configuration>
          <executions>
            <execution>
              <id>javadoc-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>
              </goals>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
          <executions>
            <execution>
              <id>source-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>
              </goals>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
          <executions>
            <!-- Copy javadoc's "element-list" file to "package-list" in order to allow         -->

            <!-- Thymeleaf's javadoc as an external link.                                       -->
            <!-- NOTE this modifies the javadoc AFTER the creation of the jar as it is not      -->

            <execution>

    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Build file locations       -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <disclaimer-files.basedir>${project.basedir}/../..</disclaimer-files.basedir>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Configure JavaDoc plugin   -->
    <!-- (Avoids JPMS issues.)      -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <maven.javadoc.source>8</maven.javadoc.source>
    <maven.javadoc.release>8</maven.javadoc.release>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- JPMS MODULE management     -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <module.name>TO_BE_SPECIFIED_BY_CHILDREN:module.name</module.name>
  </properties>

  <build>

    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>${disclaimer-files.basedir}</directory>
        <targetPath>META-INF</targetPath>
        <includes>
          <include>LICENSE.txt</include>
          <include>NOTICE.txt</include>
        </includes>
      </resource>
    </resources>

    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
          <configuration>
            <!-- Configuration will be inherited from thymeleaf-parent. At this level we will   -->
            <!-- add some additional properties.                                                -->
            <archive>
              <manifestEntries>
                <!-- Setting this automatic module name will fix the module name used by        -->
                <!-- thymeleaf even if the library is not yet fully modularised.                -->
                <!-- NOTE this will have to be set at each of the modules' pom.xml files.       -->
                <Automatic-Module-Name>${module.name}</Automatic-Module-Name>
              </manifestEntries>
            </archive>
          </configuration>
        </plugin>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
          <configuration>
            <show>protected</show>
            <noqualifier>java.lang</noqualifier>
            <source>${maven.javadoc.source}</source>
            <release>${maven.javadoc.release}</release>
            <overview>${basedir}/src/main/javadoc/overview.html</overview>
            <javadocDirectory>${basedir}/src/main/javadoc</javadocDirectory>
            <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}</outputDirectory>
            <doclint>all,-missing</doclint>
          </configuration>
          <executions>
            <execution>
              <id>javadoc-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>
              </goals>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
          <executions>
            <execution>
              <id>source-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>
              </goals>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
          <executions>
            <!-- Copy javadoc's "element-list" file to "package-list" in order to allow         -->
            <!-- projects using versions of the javadoc tool < JDK9 to properly link to         -->
            <!-- Thymeleaf's javadoc as an external link.                                       -->
            <!-- NOTE this modifies the javadoc AFTER the creation of the jar as it is not      -->
            <!-- possible to do so by previously configuring javadoc:javadoc in the             -->

            <!-- second execution of the javadoc tool in the javadoc:jar goal.                  -->
            <execution>

              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>run</goal>

            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>

  </build>

    <module>thymeleaf-spring5</module>
    <module>thymeleaf-spring6</module>
    <module>thymeleaf-extras-springsecurity5</module>
    <module>thymeleaf-extras-springsecurity6</module>
    <module>testing</module>
  </modules>

</project>

        final ExpressionParsingState decomposition = ExpressionParsingUtil.decompose(input);

        final ExpressionParsingState result = ExpressionParsingUtil.compose(decomposition);

    private static final int NEW_LEN = NEW_ARRAY.length;
    private static final char[] PARAM_ARRAY = "marap".toCharArray(); // Inverted "param"
    private static final int PARAM_LEN = PARAM_ARRAY.length;


    public static boolean mightNeedExpressionObjects(final String expression) {
        return expression.indexOf('#') >= 0;
    }


    /*
     * @since 3.0.12
     */
    public static boolean containsExternalAccess(final String expression) {

        /*
         * Checks whether the expression contains instantiation of objects ("new SomeClass") or makes use of
         * static methods ("@SomeClass@") as both are forbidden in certain contexts in restricted mode.
         */

        final int explen = exp.length();

        int ni = 0; // index for computing position in the NEW_ARRAY
        int pi = 0; // index for computing position in the PARAM_ARRAY
        int si = -1;
        char c;
        while (n-- != 0) {

            c = exp.charAt(n);

            // When checking for the "new" keyword, we need to identify that it is not a part of a larger
            // identifier, i.e. there is whitespace after it and no character that might be a part of an
            // identifier before it.
            if (ni < NEW_LEN
                    && c == NEW_ARRAY[ni]
                    && (ni > 0 || ((n + 1 < explen) && Character.isWhitespace(exp.charAt(n + 1))))) {
                ni++;
                if (ni == NEW_LEN && (n == 0 || !isSafeIdentifierChar(exp.charAt(n - 1)))) {
                    return true; // we found an object instantiation
                }
                continue;
            }

            if (ni > 0) {
                // We 'restart' the matching counter just in case we had a partial match
                n += ni;
                ni = 0;
                if (si < n) {
                    // This has to be restarted too
                    si = -1;
                }
                continue;
            }

            ni = 0;

            // When checking for the "param" keyword, we need to identify that it is not a part of a larger
            // identifier.
            if (pi < PARAM_LEN
                    && c == PARAM_ARRAY[pi]
                    && (pi > 0 || ((n + 1 < explen) && !isSafeIdentifierChar(exp.charAt(n + 1))))) {
                pi++;
                if (pi == PARAM_LEN && (n == 0 || !isSafeIdentifierChar(exp.charAt(n - 1)))) {
                    return true; // we found a param access
                }
                continue;
            }

            if (pi > 0) {
                // We 'restart' the matching counter just in case we had a partial match
                n += pi;
                pi = 0;
                continue;
            }

            pi = 0;

            if (c == '@') {
                if (si > n) {
                    return true;
                }
                si = n;
            } else if (si > n && !(Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(c) || Character.isWhitespace(c) || c == '.')) {
                si = -1;
            }

        }

        return false;

    }


    private static boolean isSafeIdentifierChar(final char c) {
        return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_';
    }





    private StandardExpressionUtils() {
        super();
    }



}

        private final char[][] pool;
        private final boolean[] allocated;
        private final int poolBufferSize;

        private BufferPool(final int poolSize, final int poolBufferSize) {

            super();

            this.allocated = new boolean[poolSize];
            this.poolBufferSize = poolBufferSize;

            for (int i = 0; i < this.pool.length; i++) {
                this.pool[i] = new char[this.poolBufferSize];
            }

            if (bufferSize != this.poolBufferSize) {

                // create it without pooling.
                return new char[bufferSize];
            }
            for (int i = 0; i < this.pool.length; i++) {
                if (!this.allocated[i]) {
                    this.allocated[i] = true;
                    return this.pool[i];
                }
            }
            return new char[bufferSize];
        }

        private synchronized void releaseBuffer(final char[] buffer) {
            if (buffer == null) {
                return;

            if (buffer.length != this.poolBufferSize) {

                return;

            for (int i = 0; i < this.pool.length; i++) {

                    return;

    public static void parseCloseElement(
            final char[] buffer,
            final int offset, final int len,
            final int line, final int col,
            final ITextHandler handler)
            throws TextParseException {

        if (len < 3 || !isCloseElementStart(buffer, offset, offset + len) || !isElementEnd(buffer, (offset + len) - 1, offset + len, false)) {
            throw new TextParseException(
                    "Could not parse as a well-formed close element: \"" + new String(buffer, offset, len) + "\"", line, col);
        }

        final int contentOffset = offset + 2;   // We add +2 because of '[/'
        final int contentLen = len - 3;         // -2 because of '[/' and another -1 because of ']'

        final int maxi = contentOffset + contentLen;

        final int[] locator = new int[] {line, col + 2};

        /*
         * Extract the element name first
         */

        final int elementNameEnd =
                TextParsingUtil.findNextWhitespaceCharWildcard(buffer, contentOffset, maxi, true, locator);

        if (elementNameEnd == -1) {
            // The buffer only contains the element name

            handler.handleCloseElementStart(
                    buffer, contentOffset, contentLen,
                    line, col);

            handler.handleCloseElementEnd(
                    buffer, contentOffset, contentLen,
                    locator[0], locator[1]);

            return;

        }


        handler.handleCloseElementStart(
                buffer, contentOffset, (elementNameEnd - contentOffset),
                line, col);


        final int wsEnd =
                TextParsingUtil.findNextNonWhitespaceCharWildcard(buffer, elementNameEnd, maxi, locator);

        if (wsEnd != -1) {
            // This is a close tag, so everything should be whitespace
            // until the end of the close tag
            throw new TextParseException(
                    "Could not parse as a well-formed closing element \"" + new String(buffer, offset, len) + "\": No attributes are allowed here", line, col);
        }


        handler.handleCloseElementEnd(
                buffer, contentOffset, (elementNameEnd - contentOffset),
                locator[0], locator[1]);

    }






    static boolean isOpenElementStart(final char[] buffer, final int offset, final int maxi) {

        final int len = maxi - offset;

        return (len > 2 &&
                    buffer[offset] == '[' &&
                    buffer[offset + 1] == '#' &&
                    isElementNameOrEnd(buffer, offset + 2, maxi));

    }


    static boolean isCloseElementStart(final char[] buffer, final int offset, final int maxi) {

        final int len = maxi - offset;

        if (len <= 2 || buffer[offset] != '[' || buffer[offset + 1] != '/') {
            return false;
        }

        final int nameStart = offset + 2;

        if (!isElementNameOrEnd(buffer, nameStart, maxi)) {
            return false;
        }

        // Scan ahead to ensure the name between '[/' and ']' contains no '/',
        // which would indicate content like [/regex/flags] rather than a close element.
        for (int i = nameStart; i < maxi; i++) {
            final char c = buffer[i];
            if (c == ']' || Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                return true;
            }
            if (c == '/') {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;

    }


    static boolean isElementEnd(final char[] buffer, final int offset, final int maxi, final boolean minimized) {

        final int len = maxi - offset;

        if (len < 1) {
            return false; // won't fit
        }

        if (minimized) {
            if (len < 2 || buffer[offset] != '/') {
                return false;
            }
            return buffer[offset + 1] == ']';
        }

        return buffer[offset] == ']';

    }




    private static boolean isElementNameOrEnd(final char[] buffer, final int offset, final int maxi) {

        if (Character.isWhitespace(buffer[offset])) {
            // We cover here the case when we don't apply an element name: [# th:something=...]
            return true;
        }

        final int len = maxi - offset;

        if (len > 1 && buffer[offset] == '/') {
            // This can still be valid if we are just closing a no-name standalone element without attributes: [#/]
            return isElementEnd(buffer, offset, maxi, true);
        }

        if (len > 0 && buffer[offset] == ']') {
            // This can still be valid if we are just closing a no-name open element without attributes: [#]
            return isElementEnd(buffer, offset, maxi, false);
        }

        // At this point the element HAS TO have a name, as we have already ruled out all possibilities that it does not.
        // The rules for an element name are basically the same, wrt allowed chars, as a normal markup (HTML,XML) element.
        // Note however that we will not be allowing a '{' just after the first # character already parsed so that we
        // don't mistake a direct output expression for an externalized message [[#{my.message}]] for an element.
        return (len > 0 &&
                buffer[offset] != '-' && buffer[offset] != '!' &&
                buffer[offset] != '/' && buffer[offset] != '?' &&
                buffer[offset] != '[' && buffer[offset] != '{' &&
                !Character.isWhitespace(buffer[offset]));

    }

    @Test
    public void testPlainTextDocumentReportsStartTextAndEnd() throws Exception {

        final RecordingHandler handler = parseDocument("Hello World", 64, 0, false);

        assertEquals(
                Arrays.asList("documentStart[1,1]", "text[1,1]:Hello World", "documentEnd[1,12]"),
                handler.events);

        assertEquals(1, handler.documentStartCount);
        assertEquals(1, handler.documentEndCount);

        // The document start event always reports the very first position of the document
        assertEquals(1, handler.startLine);
        assertEquals(1, handler.startCol);

        // The document end position has been fast-forwarded past the trailing text that was reported
        assertEquals(1, handler.endLine);
        assertEquals(12, handler.endCol);

        // The reported timings must be coherent with the event timestamps
        assertTrue(handler.endTimeNanos >= handler.startTimeNanos);
        assertEquals(handler.endTimeNanos - handler.startTimeNanos, handler.totalTimeNanos);

    }


    @Test
    public void testEmptyDocumentProducesNoTextEvents() throws Exception {

        final RecordingHandler handler = parseDocument("", 32, 0, false);

        assertEquals(Arrays.asList("documentStart[1,1]", "documentEnd[1,1]"), handler.events);
        assertEquals(1, handler.documentStartCount);
        assertEquals(1, handler.documentEndCount);
        assertEquals(1, handler.endLine);
        assertEquals(1, handler.endCol);

    }


    @Test
    public void testTextIsReportedAsOneEventRegardlessOfLineBreaks() throws Exception {

        final RecordingHandler handler = parseDocument("line1\nline2\n", 64, 0, false);

        // Text is reported incrementally, so newlines inside it do not split the event
        assertEquals(
                Arrays.asList("documentStart[1,1]", "text[1,1]:line1\\nline2\\n", "documentEnd[3,1]"),
                handler.events);
        assertEquals(3, handler.endLine);
        assertEquals(1, handler.endCol);

    }

        assertEquals(3, handler.endCol);

  <artifactId>thymeleaf-lib</artifactId>

  <name>thymeleaf lib</name>

  <properties>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Build file locations       -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <disclaimer-files.basedir>${project.basedir}/../..</disclaimer-files.basedir>
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <!-- Configure JavaDoc plugin   -->
    <!-- (Avoids JPMS issues.)      -->
    <!-- =========================  -->
    <maven.javadoc.source>8</maven.javadoc.source>

    <!-- =========================  -->

    <!-- =========================  -->
    <module.name>TO_BE_SPECIFIED_BY_CHILDREN:module.name</module.name>
  </properties>

  <build>

    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>${disclaimer-files.basedir}</directory>
        <targetPath>META-INF</targetPath>
        <includes>
          <include>LICENSE.txt</include>
          <include>NOTICE.txt</include>
        </includes>
      </resource>
    </resources>

    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>

        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
          <configuration>
            <!-- Configuration will be inherited from thymeleaf-parent. At this level we will   -->
            <!-- add some additional properties.                                                -->
            <archive>
              <manifestEntries>

            <execution>
              <id>javadoc-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>
              </goals>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

          <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
          <executions>
            <execution>
              <id>source-jar</id>
              <phase>package</phase>
              <goals>
                <goal>jar</goal>

              </configuration>
            </execution>
          </executions>
        </plugin>

    <module>thymeleaf-spring6</module>
    <module>thymeleaf-extras-springsecurity5</module>
    <module>thymeleaf-extras-springsecurity6</module>
    <module>testing</module>
  </modules>

        }

package org.thymeleaf.util;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.util.Calendar;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.TimeZone;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertAll;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

class DateUtilsCreateTests {


    @Test
    void createsCalendarFromNumericObjectsUsingAllProvidedComponents() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                Integer.valueOf(2024),
                Long.valueOf(2),
                Short.valueOf((short) 29),
                Byte.valueOf((byte) 13),
                new BigDecimal("45"),
                BigInteger.valueOf(30),
                Double.valueOf(123.0),
                TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"),
                Locale.US);

        assertNotNull(calendar);
        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2024, Calendar.FEBRUARY, 29, 13, 45, 30, 123);
        assertEquals("UTC", calendar.getTimeZone().getID());
    }


    @Test
    void createsCalendarFromStringRepresentationsAndTimeZoneId() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                "2020", "02", "29", "12", "30", "45", "006",
                "GMT+05:30", Locale.US);

        assertNotNull(calendar);
        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2020, Calendar.FEBRUARY, 29, 12, 30, 45, 6);
        assertEquals("GMT+05:30", calendar.getTimeZone().getID());
        assertEquals((5 * 60 + 30) * 60 * 1000, calendar.getTimeZone().getRawOffset());
    }


    @Test
    void appliesBothExplicitTimeZoneAndLocale() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                2024, 6, 15, 10, 20, 30, 400,
                TimeZone.getTimeZone("GMT+05:30"), Locale.FRANCE);

        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2024, Calendar.JUNE, 15, 10, 20, 30, 400);
        assertEquals("GMT+05:30", calendar.getTimeZone().getID());
        assertEquals((5 * 60 + 30) * 60 * 1000, calendar.getTimeZone().getRawOffset());
        assertEquals(Calendar.MONDAY, calendar.getFirstDayOfWeek());
    }


    @Test
    void appliesExplicitLocaleWithoutExplicitTimeZone() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                2024, 6, 15, 10, 20, 30, 400,
                null, Locale.FRANCE);

        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2024, Calendar.JUNE, 15, 10, 20, 30, 400);
        assertEquals(Calendar.MONDAY, calendar.getFirstDayOfWeek());
        assertEquals(TimeZone.getDefault().getID(), calendar.getTimeZone().getID());
    }


    @Test
    void defaultsMissingTimeComponentsToZero() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                2023, 12, 31, null, null, null, null, null, null);

        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2023, Calendar.DECEMBER, 31, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    }


    @Test
    void defaultsMillisecondToZeroWhenSecondIsProvided() {

        final Calendar calendar = DateUtils.create(
                2023, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, null, null, null);

        assertCalendarFields(calendar, 2023, Calendar.JANUARY, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0);
    }


    @Test
    void supportsTimeBoundaryValues() {

        final Calendar startOfDay = DateUtils.create(
                2000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, "UTC", Locale.US);
        final Calendar endOfDay = DateUtils.create(
                1999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, 999, "UTC", Locale.US);

        assertAll(
                () -> assertCalendarFields(startOfDay, 2000, Calendar.JANUARY, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                () -> assertCalendarFields(endOfDay, 1999, Calendar.DECEMBER, 31, 23, 59, 59, 999));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsNullRequiredDateComponents() {

        assertAll(
                () -> {
                    final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                            IllegalArgumentException.class,
                            () -> DateUtils.create(null, 1, 1, null, null, null, null, null, null));
                    assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("null year (null)"));
                },
                () -> {
                    final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                            IllegalArgumentException.class,
                            () -> DateUtils.create(2024, null, 1, null, null, null, null, null, null));
                    assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("month (null)"));
                },
                () -> {
                    final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                            IllegalArgumentException.class,
                            () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, null, null, null, null, null, null, null));
                    assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("day (null)"));
                });
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsRequiredDateComponentsThatCannotBeParsedAsNumbers() {

        assertAll(
                () -> assertThrows(
                        IllegalArgumentException.class,
                        () -> DateUtils.create("not-a-year", 1, 1, null, null, null, null, null, null)),
                () -> assertThrows(
                        IllegalArgumentException.class,
                        () -> DateUtils.create(2024, "", 1, null, null, null, null, null, null)),
                () -> assertThrows(
                        IllegalArgumentException.class,
                        () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, "1x", null, null, null, null, null, null)));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsHourWithoutMinute() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, 12, null, null, null, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("hour (12)"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("minute (null)"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("either both null or non-null"));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsMinuteWithoutHour() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, null, 30, null, null, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("hour (null)"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("minute (30)"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("either both null or non-null"));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsSecondWithoutHourAndMinute() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, null, null, 30, null, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("null hour and minute"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("non-null second and/or millisecond"));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsMillisecondWithoutHourAndMinute() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, null, null, null, 500, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("null hour and minute"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("non-null second and/or millisecond"));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsMillisecondWithoutSecond() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, 12, 30, null, 500, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("null second"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("non-null millisecond"));
    }


    @Test
    void rejectsNonNumericHourWhenMinuteIsPresent() {

        final IllegalArgumentException exception = assertThrows(
                IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> DateUtils.create(2024, 1, 1, "not-an-hour", 30, null, null, null, null));

        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("hour (null)"));
        assertTrue(exception.getMessage().contains("either both null or non-null"));
    }


    private static void assertCalendarFields(
            final Calendar calendar,
            final int year,
            final int month,
            final int day,
            final int hour,
            final int minute,
            final int second,
            final int millisecond) {

        assertAll(
                () -> assertEquals(year, calendar.get(Calendar.YEAR)),
                () -> assertEquals(month, calendar.get(Calendar.MONTH)),
                () -> assertEquals(day, calendar.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH)),
                () -> assertEquals(hour, calendar.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY)),
                () -> assertEquals(minute, calendar.get(Calendar.MINUTE)),
                () -> assertEquals(second, calendar.get(Calendar.SECOND)),
                () -> assertEquals(millisecond, calendar.get(Calendar.MILLISECOND)));
    }

}

        assertNotNull(result);
        assertTrue(result.isEmpty());
        assertListIsUnmodifiable(result);
    }

    @Test
    void nonIterableNonMapNonArrayValuesAreReturnedAsSingleElementLists() {
        final Object marker = new Object();
        final List<Object> markerResult = EvaluationUtils.evaluateAsList(marker);

        assertEquals(1, markerResult.size());
        assertSame(marker, markerResult.get(0));
        assertListIsUnmodifiable(markerResult);

        final List<Object> stringResult = EvaluationUtils.evaluateAsList("text");
        assertEquals(Collections.singletonList("text"), stringResult);
        assertListIsUnmodifiable(stringResult);
    }

    @Test
    void iterableIsCopiedInIterationOrderIncludingDuplicatesAndNulls() {
        final Object first = new Object();
        final Iterable<Object> source = Arrays.asList(first, null, first);

        final List<Object> result = EvaluationUtils.evaluateAsList(source);

        assertEquals(3, result.size());
        assertSame(first, result.get(0));
        assertNull(result.get(1));
        assertSame(first, result.get(2));
        assertNotSame(source, result);
        assertListIsUnmodifiable(result);
    }

    @Test
    void iterableResultIsASnapshotOfTheSource() {
        final List<String> source = new ArrayList<String>();
        source.add("original");

        final List<Object> result = EvaluationUtils.evaluateAsList(source);
        source.add("later");
        source.set(0, "changed");

        assertEquals(Collections.singletonList("original"), result);
    }

        assertListIsUnmodifiable(emptyPrimitiveArray);
